title: Muscle & Strength: The Tactical Physique
author: Mithosphere
desc:
INTRODUCTION
The primary purpose of this program is to bridge the gap between functional athletic performance and aesthetic physical design. Developed by strength specialist Brad Borland, this 10-week intermediate program shifts focus away from traditional bodybuilding splits and redirects it toward building a body that moves and performs cohesively as a single, functional unit.

The program aims to develop comprehensive, real-world capabilities alongside an impressive physique by targeting six key physical pillars:
- Raw Strength & Hypertrophy: Utilizing heavy compound movements and strategic supersets to maximize muscular cross-sectional size and power.
- Power & Explosiveness: Training the body to move weight quickly and deliberately to improve immediate force production.
- Muscular & Cardiovascular Endurance: Transitioning from traditional low-intensity cardio to HIIT and high-rep endurance sequences.
- Speed, Agility, & Mobility: Incorporating sprinting intervals and agility work to build directional control.
- Injury Prevention & Balance: Prioritizing dynamic warm-ups and unilateral training to eliminate strength imbalances.

TIPS TO ACHIEVE YOU BEST PHYSIQUE
To successfully transition to this holistic approach and unlock your highest physical potential, keep these essential training parameters in mind:
- Commit to the Timeline: Give the program at least 4 to 6 weeks before expecting major changes.
- Control the Pace: Keep your workouts under 60 minutes by strictly managing rest periods.
- Maintain True Intensity: Supersets are not an excuse to go light; challenge yourself with heavy weights while enforcing strict textbook form.
- Manage Stamina: If you run out of energy, slightly reduce total sets rather than sacrificing intensity, and gradually build your endurance over time.

INTEGRATED DYNAMIC WARM-UP & STRETCHING
To prepare your joints and central nervous system for intense stress, every workout must begin with this mandatory prehab sequence to enhance performance and protect structural longevity:
- Foam Rolling (5-10 mins): Roll the calves, IT bands, hamstrings, quads, glutes, and upper back to release myofascial tightness.
- Dynamic warm-up/stretching. The following will be performed prior to each training session for better performance and a safer workout.
++ Push-ups: 20 reps
++ Burpees: 10 reps
++ Walking lunges (long stride): 20 paces
++ Lying ab windshield wipers: 10 reps per side
++ Jump squats: 10 reps
++ Inverted rows: 10 reps
++ Side lunges: 10 reps per side

CONCLUSION
Ultimately, the workout mirrors the training needs of military special forces, firefighters, and police officers. It builds a resilient posterior chain, a stable core, and overall physical preparedness, ensuring you not only look athletic but possess the practical capability to lift, push, pull, and perform optimally under stress outside of the gym.
